test_title: PYST 38: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - Mathematics (Held On: 20 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: An article is sold for x. If it is sold at 40% of this price, there is a loss of 50%. What is the percentage profit when it is sold for ₹x?
solution:
**Given:**

Article selling price (SP) = ₹x

If sold at 40% of SP, Loss = 50%

**Formula used:**

Cost Price (CP) = SP at Loss ÷ (1 - Loss%)

Profit% = [(Selling Price - Cost Price) ÷ Cost Price] × 100

**Calculation:**

Selling Price at 40% = 40% of x = 0.4x

Loss = 50% = 0.5

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = 0.4x ÷ (1 - 0.5)

⇒ CP = 0.4x ÷ 0.5

⇒ CP = 0.8x

Now, Profit% when sold at ₹x:

Profit% = [(Selling Price - Cost Price) ÷ Cost Price] × 100

⇒ Profit% = [(x - 0.8x) ÷ 0.8x] × 100

⇒ Profit% = [0.2x ÷ 0.8x] × 100

⇒ Profit% = 0.25 × 100

⇒ Profit% = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**
